about: What Davy does, what is being built and what comes next. A change that ships or starts an item updates this file in the same commit; node site/tools/roadmap.cjs then rewrites the site.

items.title: A cold tier for old logs
items.what: Old days of logs become compressed files that stay searchable, on the local disk now and on object storage next.

items.title: Sign in with any OIDC provider
items.what: People sign in to the web UI through the identity provider the team already uses.

items.title: Agent tokens with a level
items.what: Each agent gets its own token with a level, read, triage or full, and only a person unlocks a change that deletes data.

items.title: An audit log of what agents changed
items.what: Every change an agent or a person makes, such as a resolved issue or a new drop rule, is recorded with who made it.

items.title: Backup and restore
items.what: One command takes a consistent copy of a running server and another brings it back.

items.title: A hosted Davy, run by us
items.what: The same Davy, for teams that would rather not run a server.

items.title: Daily quotas and spike protection
items.what: Each project gets a daily limit, so one runaway app cannot fill the disk for the others.

items.title: A usage page in the web UI
items.what: One page shows the disk used and free, the day it fills, what each project sends and where it could take less.

items.title: Agents propose drop rules
items.what: An agent stages a drop rule that only counts what it would drop, and a person makes it live.

items.title: Drop rules with shadow mode
items.what: Log lines nobody needs are dropped before they are stored, after a shadow run shows what a rule would drop.

items.title: A savings view
items.what: Davy lists the log patterns with the most bytes, logs kept longer than anyone reads and the noisiest issues, with the command that frees the space.

items.title: Search history
items.what: Davy records the log searches people and agents run, so it can tell which logs nobody reads.

items.title: Discard an issue
items.what: A noisy issue stops storing new events and only counts them.

items.title: Davy watches itself
items.what: Davy stores its own warnings and errors in a project of its own, where they can be searched like any app's.

items.title: Logs from Vercel
items.what: A Vercel log drain sends a deployment's logs straight to Davy, with its signature checked.

items.title: A disk forecast
items.what: Davy tells you the day the disk fills at the current rate, per project, from the first hour of data.

items.title: Usage counters
items.what: Davy counts what each project sends per day and signal, and keeps the counts for 400 days.

items.title: Log patterns
items.what: Log lines are grouped by shape, so you see which kinds of line fill the logs.

items.title: Scrubbing on by default
items.what: Passwords, keys, card numbers and IP addresses are removed on the server before anything is stored.

items.title: Retention per project
items.what: Each project keeps its logs and its errors for as many days as it needs.

items.title: Connect an app in one command
items.what: One command prints the SDK setup for an app and a command that sends a test event.

items.title: Release health and user feedback
items.what: Davy shows crash-free sessions per release, and what users wrote in the feedback widget next to the issue.

items.title: Cron check-ins
items.what: A scheduled job that reports in becomes a monitor that alerts when a run is late or fails.

items.title: A web UI for one team
items.what: People read issues, logs and uptime in a browser, behind a password.

items.title: Signed releases
items.what: Every release ships with checksums, an SBOM per binary, build provenance and a signed image.

items.title: Install by prompt
items.what: An agent installs Davy and connects an app from one prompt.

items.title: Uptime checks and alerts
items.what: HTTP checks and heartbeats alert by e-mail, Slack or a signed webhook when something stops answering.

items.title: Source maps
items.what: Minified JavaScript stack traces point back at the lines you wrote.

items.title: Tools for agents
items.what: An MCP server and a CLI let an agent search errors and logs, read an issue and mark it fixed.

items.title: Logs
items.what: Logs from OpenTelemetry, Logtail shippers and Sentry's logger, with full-text search, on a store picked by a published benchmark.

items.title: Errors from the Sentry SDKs
items.what: Point an existing Sentry SDK at Davy and errors arrive grouped into issues.
